reasons.B: Closest in movement and stance: long balanced sentences joined by semicolons, reflective hedges ('I suspect', 'it may be', 'it seems to me', 'perhaps'), direct address to the reader and a quiet aphoristic close, all at about the passage's density.
reasons.A: Similar formal register and long periodic sentences with 'it seems to me' and a dash aside, but the tone turns drier and faintly ironic ('rather fond of doing it'), with fewer semicolons and less of the tentative, confiding hedging.
reasons.C: Short, plain, modern sentences, colon lists, quoted examples and confident prescriptions ('First... Second...'); little hedging and no semicolon rhythm, so it reads least like the author.
